summary: No state facility, expression or ordinance law was documented for Roraima: the national protective-but-porous framework applies unchanged. On record it sits at the safe extreme of the Brazilian map — no killings of trans people were found recorded in the state for 2024, and in 2025 it falls in the lowest national band (0-3 cases) — though the dossier stresses these are floors from systematic under-counting and a single case would swing the rate in so small a state. Federally administered indigenous territories with parallel community authority lie within Roraima; no trans-specific evidence was found for them.

sources.summary: Wikipedia overview of LGBTQ rights in Brazil: STF rulings give gender identity/expression protection without surgery or court order, the 2019 equating of LGBTphobia with racism, and non-binary birth-certificate recognition handled case-by-case per federative unit — Roraima's row notes a 2025 free judicial action permitting trans and non-binary rectifications, with no state statute establishing the option. Useful as the national legal backdrop; no state criminalisation.

Outright International Brazil country overview (updated 12 March 2026): marriage equality since 2013 under repeal pressure, 2019 STF hate-crime equivalence, self-determination gender markers, world's highest absolute trans-murder toll with interior vs capital geography, conservative-Congress anti-LGBTIQ surge against a pro-rights executive — the national frame applied uniformly in Roraima.

Law-firm expat guide (updated 5 April 2026) to LGBTQ+ legal rights in Brazil: no comprehensive federal anti-discrimination statute but progressive STF jurisprudence (marriage, adoption, marker changes without surgery, phobia-as-racism); explicitly warns the framework is 'progressive on paper and uneven in practice', with protections concentrated in major cities — the interior-unevenness caveat that covers Roraima.

localsOnly: Birth-certificate rectification for trans and non-binary people in Roraima runs through free judicial action (2025), not a state administrative channel.
